## Rectify a mask and close fluid faces against solids (`boundary-condition/internal/*; vars["solid"]`) {#sec-ch11-solids}

<!-- PROVENANCE
pin: snapy@e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0
status: draft
-->

Local symbols: $D_i(b,l)$ is the minimum flip count after processing $i$ mask entries, ending with bit
$b$ and capped run length $l$; $m_b$ is its required run length (counts). Bits and $\mathrm{cost}_i(b)$, the candidate flip cost at position $i$, are dimensionless.
$\mathsf H$ is the dimensionless reflection matrix, distinct from the Riemann eigenvector matrix $\mathsf R$.
These symbols are proposed in the notation issue.

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
A static mask selects solid cells. Directional minimum-flip sweeps repair thin runs; mirrored face states and masked implicit rows isolate the fluid segments.
Default: max-iter 5; density $10^3\ \mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$; pressure $10^9\ \mathrm{Pa}$.
Order: exact discrete operation or local derivation below; coupled solver order not measured.
:::

### Derivation

At a single fluid-solid interface, copy the fluid reconstructed state to the solid side and negate its normal
velocity. This yields the reflecting pair derived in @sec-ch11-reflecting, now at a face of a staircase mask.
`InternalBoundaryImpl::forward` ([`internal_boundary.cpp:47-95`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/internal_boundary.cpp#L47-L95)) applies that rule after reconstructing the fluid side. A face with
solid on both sides has no fluid flux interpretation in this argument.

The rectification problem on one line minimizes the count of changed zeros. Set $m_0=3$ and $m_1=2$.
A candidate equal to the original bit costs zero; changing zero to one costs one; changing one to zero has
infinite cost. Start with $D_0(0,0)=D_0(1,0)=0$ and all other states infinite. Extending the current bit increments
its run length, capped at $m_b$. Switching to the other bit starts length one only if the previous length is
zero (the start) or at least $m_b$. For every permitted predecessor, update the candidate state by the minimum
of its existing cost and predecessor cost plus the flip cost:

$$
D_{i+1}(b,l)\leftarrow\min\bigl(D_{i+1}(b,l),D_i(b_{\mathrm{old}},l_{\mathrm{old}})
+\mathrm{cost}_i(b)\bigr).
$$ {#eq-ch11-solids-dp}

`compute_min_flips` ([`flip_zero_impl.h:24-198`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/flip_zero_impl.h#L24-L198)) implements @eq-ch11-solids-dp and retains the predecessor only on a strict
improvement. The terminal run must also reach its minimum. Every admissible prefix ends in one of these
states; induction on prefix length shows the recurrence retains the smallest possible cost. Backtracking
returns a minimizing line. This proves a line optimum, not a global multidimensional optimum after alternating
sweeps. `flip_zero_cpu` ({{< code src/bc/bc_dispatch.cpp flip_zero_cpu >}}) sums line costs atomically. C5 compares an independent dynamic program
with exhaustive enumeration for every binary line of lengths two through eight.

For the partial implicit system, $\mathsf H=\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,1)$ on density, normal momentum and
energy rows. A reflecting ghost increment is $\mathsf H\Delta\mathbf U_i$. Substitution into the lower
neighbour block contributes $\mathsf B_i\mathsf H\Delta\mathbf U_i$ to the diagonal; the upper side contributes
$\mathsf C_i\mathsf H\Delta\mathbf U_i$. Thus

$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf A_i&\leftarrow\mathsf A_i+\mathsf B_i\mathsf H,\\
\mathsf A_i&\leftarrow\mathsf A_i+\mathsf C_i\mathsf H.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch11-solids-closure}

Apply each row only at its relevant fluid boundary. `Bnd` ({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_partial_impl.h vic_assemble_partial_impl >}}) implements
@eq-ch11-solids-closure; `solid_lower` ({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_partial_impl.h vic_assemble_partial_impl >}}) also mirrors the base state used in the face Jacobian.
A solid row has diagonal identity divided by $\Delta t$ and zero neighbours (`setIdentity`, {{< code src/implicit/implicit_dispatch.cpp vic_assemble_partial_cpu >}}).
The masked RHS is zero (`forward_masked`, {{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_apply_implicit_correction >}}), so that row has zero solved increment. C6 verifies the
block substitution algebra. The full-system closure has an additional nonperiodic guard ({{< code src/implicit/vic_assemble_full_impl.h vic_assemble_full_impl >}});
this derivation does not assert an untested periodic-solid combination.

The report-only checks are `src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.py`; their current output is
`src/snapy_report/ch11/boundary_check.out`. They do not call a snapy kernel.

### Numerical method

The mask shape is the three spatial extents. Rectification makes it contiguous (which may alias an already
contiguous input), fills all resolved ghost slabs with ones, sweeps x1/x2/x3 and alternates traversal direction
until a sweep has no flips. Exhausting `max-iter` throws. Optional callbacks apply afterward.

Initialization saves separate primitive/conserved fill states with velocity or momentum zeroed. Primitive
placeholders use the configured density and pressure, zero velocity and zero composition. During a stage,
face states mirror at solid interfaces; the time-step sound speed in solid cells is replaced by $10^{-8}\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$.
The implicit solve masks solid increments and requires an unsplit x1 column. After RK combination only hydro
conserved cells are refilled; the gravity-work fixer excludes solid mass. Staircase geometry is cell-aligned,
not a cut-cell representation, and no geometric convergence order is measured.

: Implementation sites for solids. {#tbl-ch11-solids-code}

1. Read max iterations and solid placeholders; require the mask shape at initialization. The anchor `max_iter` is in {{< code src/bc/internal_boundary.cpp InternalBoundaryOptionsImpl::from_yaml overload=2 >}}.
2. Mark ghost slabs solid, perform directional minimum-flip sweeps, reject nonconvergence, then apply optional mask callbacks. The anchor `rectify_solid` is in {{< code src/bc/rectify_solid.cpp InternalBoundaryImpl::rectify_solid >}}.
3. Save fill states, mark primitives, mirror reconstructed interface states and mask the implicit system. The anchor `mark_prim_solid_` is in [`internal_boundary.cpp:47-95`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/bc/internal_boundary.cpp#L47-L95).
4. Refill hydro after stage combination and exclude solids from gravity-fixer mass. The anchor `apply_boundaries` is in {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
The per-line optimum does not make the multidimensional repaired mask globally minimal. Exceeding the
iteration limit can reject a mask whose last permitted sweep still changes entries. The mask and fill states
are static. The cited stage refill only restores hydro, not passive scalars ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}); scalar-solid isolation
needs runtime evidence. Diffusion and solid placeholders require separate coefficient analysis; no quantitative
placeholder contamination measurement is reused here. Implicit x1 decomposition is explicitly rejected ({{< code src/hydro/hydro.cpp HydroImpl::_apply_implicit_correction >}}).

Untested switch combinations remain subject to @sec-ch12-matrix. No new CPU, CUDA or multi-rank solver result is claimed.
:::
